fix.summary: Hardened TestF0005NameToClassMapping.test_register_class_recorded_alongside_instance from an N8 (existence-only / vacuous) non-gate into a real behavioral gate. The old test asserted only that unregister() returns True and that list_registered() == [] after register_class() alone — it never verified that register(instance) stored the concrete class in _provider_classes. The new test calls register(instance) and then directly asserts, via getattr+cast (the project-established pattern for accessing private methods without triggering reportPrivateUsage), that _provider_classes[ANTHROPIC] is ConcreteTestProvider. fix.summary: Hardened test_memory_text_shows_gb_values from an N9 string-presence proxy (asserting only "GB" and "%" substrings) into a real numeric-value gate. The rewritten test calls get_xpu_memory_info(0) as an independent oracle, forces a synchronous dialog refresh via getattr(xpu_dialog, "_refresh_memory")(), then parses the actual label text with re.fullmatch to extract alloc_gb, total_gb, and pct values. It asserts each parsed value is within ±1 GB / ±2 pp of the oracle-derived values, covering legitimate VRAM churn between the oracle call and the refresh. A swapped-allocated/total regression, an NaN format, or any missing field causes the regex match to return None or the numeric assertions to fail. The total==0 branch is also explicitly gated to "Unable to determine memory size" so the test is non-vacuous on degenerate hardware. Added import re at the top of the file.

findings_addressed.category: N9 log/string-presence proxy — asserted only 'GB' and '%' substrings, not the actual numeric alloc/total/pct values
findings_addressed.oracle: get_xpu_memory_info(0) — the same backend function the production dialog calls; alloc_gb and total_gb are independently computed as allocated/BYTES_PER_GB and total/BYTES_PER_GB; pct = int(allocated/total*100); regex re.fullmatch enforces exact format

falsifiability.note: On any hardware where allocated < total (e.g., 2 GB used of 8 GB), the mutated alloc_gb equals total_gb (~8.0), but the oracle's expected_alloc_gb is ~2.0. abs(8.0 - 2.0) = 6.0 > 1.0 tolerance, so the assertion fails. The old test passed because '8.00' still contains 'GB'.
